# Secret Manager

> A lightweight, self-hosted secret manager. Store a secret, share it with a
> teammate, and read it back from any machine. It runs as one container that
> brings its own database and its own accounts: no identity provider, no
> outbound network access, no third party involved.

Open source under Apache 2.0. Current release: v0.7.5.

Run it:

    docker run -d -p 8000:8000 -v secretmgr-data:/data \
      ghcr.io/clement880101/secret-manager:latest

The CLI is a single binary under 10 MB with no runtime to install, published
for Linux, macOS and Windows on the releases page.

## What it is

- Self-hosted. Anywhere a container runs: a VPS, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, a laptop.
- Bundles SQLite so a single container needs nothing else. Point `DB_URL` at Postgres to run multiple replicas.
- Its own accounts and tokens. Nothing is registered with any other service.
- Secret values are encrypted at rest with Fernet (AES-128-CBC + HMAC-SHA256) under `SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.
- Secrets are shared per key between accounts, and reads are recorded in a per-account audit trail.
- Replicas hold no state in process memory, so scaling needs no session affinity.

## What it is not

It is deliberately smaller than Vault or a cloud secrets service: no policy
language, no identity provider integration, no agent, no dynamic credentials.
The trade is far less to run and far less to learn, for far fewer features.
